body.statement:
Proposition 1 of Stoye2007ManyTreatments characterizes the many-treatment minimax-regret allocation correspondence and value as the argmin and minimum over \(q\in\Delta_K\) of
\[
 \max_{a\in\mathcal A}\left\{(1-q_a)U_{ax}-\sum_{c\neq a}q_cL_{cx}\right\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Consider the following zero-sum game between the decision maker and Nature: (i) The decision maker chooses a treatment rule δ ∈ Δ_(T−1). Nature chooses a potentially mixed strategy σ ∈ Δ_S, that is, a distribution over states of the world. (iii) The decision maker's loss is R(δ,s) ≡ max_t {μ_t} − ∑_t δ_t μ_t. Both players maximize expected utility. Then there exist convex sets D* ⊆ Δ_(T−1) and S* ⊆ Δ_S s.t. (δ*,σ*) is a Nash equilibrium of the game iff (δ*,σ*) ∈ D* × S*; furthermore, D* is the set of minimax regret treatment rules. Thus, Nature always has a best response in the set {s_t}_(t=1)^T as defined above.

attestation.note: Literal transcription with notation normalized to Unicode from the author's preprint, proof of Proposition 1 on pp. 4--5; the preceding definition on p. 3 defines s_t as treatment t at its upper bound and all other treatments at their lower bounds. Title/authorship match the Econometric Theory article and DOI 10.1017/S0266466607070089. Source: https://stoye.economics.cornell.edu/docs/ManyTreatments.pdf
